findings.title: A replacing restore lays the archive's ledger over the live one
findings.intended: spec 213 FR-043 (the ledger survives a snapshot); SNP-I3.6 (after a restore the ledger holds one history whose records and head agree); SYS-I5 (the ledger only grows); ADR-0013 (redacted content leaves history); decisions.md HD-1801 (treat the archive's history as a unit; refuse divergent histories before mutation; keep current redaction obligations).
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-ledger-overlay, AUDITC): ledger enabled, commit seq 2 (c18:L1), save, commit seq 3 (c18:L2, retry key c18-k2), replacing restore of the older archive: meta after restore {'head_id': 'ebae4dc3dfb811f1b3edf277e9aab529', 'head_seq': 2, 'max_ops': 50000, 'ok': True, 'recon_bound': 250000, 'state': 'enabled', 'strict': False}; record (3,1) still present: [1]; LedgerRevision seqs [1, 2, 3]; idem binding c18-k2 = '\x03\x04\x03B\x01de63550c92cde590c0b3685718c468739957a52a0fc9cc4ac0b69b089ee8c653'; the next commit -> {'error': 'LedgerInconsistencyError: revision row save failed: ERROR #5805: ID key not unique for extent \'Graph.KG.LedgerRevision\' : \'^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD(3)\' exists. Id counter location = \'"^Graph.KG.LedgerRevisionD"\'', 'ok': False}; a retry of c18-k2 -> {'head_seq': 2, 'replayed': True, 'seq': 3}; verify -> equal. Redaction half: a tenant node c18t|x with property secret committed, archived, erased (delete_nodes_by_prefix) and redacted; records after redaction [{'attr': '', 'digest': '3b2fff558a9c0868e7a9e8274446c3fa0a86327f09d812aa05cdd53d59b9858c', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 1, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'create_node', 'seq': 2}, {'attr': '', 'digest': 'c81fabeb686b8b9ae288d6ac215276928ba0e15cd67019213a07d837cd89d4b2', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 2, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'add_label', 'seq': 2}, {'attr': '', 'digest': 'f0be49eb039eeeb69dbf0014ccb208c777ff62a920e6f7db4b86f2e5d921cad5', 'entity_id': 'None', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': None, 'op': 'redacted', 'ordinal': 3, 'prior': None, 'redacted_op': 'set_prop', 'seq': 2}]; after a replacing restore of the pre-redaction archive the same revision's records are [{'attr': '', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': '', 'op': 'create_node', 'ordinal': 1, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}, {'attr': 'C18T', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': '', 'op': 'add_label', 'ordinal': 2, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}, {'attr': 'secret', 'entity_id': 'c18t|x', 'entity_kind': 'node', 'flags': [], 'graph': None, 'new': 'c18-sensitive', 'op': 'set_prop', 'ordinal': 3, 'prior': None, 'seq': 2}] (content back: True) while redactedRev marks ['2'] remain. Models: cmc-restore-as-built-history (expected-violation, 39 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-restore-as-built-grows (expected-violation, 39 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-restore-as-built-commit (expected-violation, 1482 states, exhaustive within bounds) (the ledger can never commit again: the leftover LedgerRevision row holds the IdKey of head+1, Ledger.cls:530-556, LedgerRevision.cls:44), cmc-restore-as-built-redaction (expected-violation, 85 states, exhaustive within bounds); reviewed cmc-restore-reviewed (pass, 891 states, exhaustive within bounds); control cmc-restore-ctl-marks (expected-violation, 85 states, exhaustive within bounds).
findings.remedy: Per HD-1801: refuse a restore whose archive history does not extend the live one, before erase_all; otherwise replace the ledger as a unit (kill ^IVG.Ledger and the ledger storage first) and re-apply live redactions (tombstones, redactedRev, idemRedacted) to the archived records.
findings.notes: The wedge (no commit possible after restoring an older archive) is stronger than the original's 'reuses sequence numbers': the IdKey on LedgerRevision.Seq refuses the next revision row, and nothing removes the leftover row.

findings.title: A merge restore guards plain tables on their first column only, and counts skipped rows as restored
findings.intended: SNP-B4.1 (a merge adds each missing row, judged by the row's own key); SNP-B4.2 (a row counts as restored only when added); USER_GUIDE.md:1151-1153 (merge=True adds to what is there).
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-merge-guard): graph c18m with 3 nodes, 2 edges, labels and props archived ({'nodes': 3, 'rdf_edges': 2, 'rdf_labels': 3, 'rdf_props': 6}); after erase and re-creating one edge, one label, one property ({'nodes': 2, 'rdf_edges': 1, 'rdf_labels': 1, 'rdf_props': 3}), merge restore left {'nodes': 3, 'rdf_edges': 1, 'rdf_labels': 1, 'rdf_props': 3} - rows missing {'nodes': 0, 'rdf_edges': 1, 'rdf_labels': 2, 'rdf_props': 3}; the result reported restored_tables {'Graph_KG.code_crosswalk': 0, 'Graph_KG.docs': 0, 'Graph_KG.embedding_registry': 0, 'Graph_KG.fhir_bridges': 0, 'Graph_KG.kg_EdgeEmbeddings': 0, 'Graph_KG.kg_NodeEmbeddings': 0, 'Graph_KG.nodes': 3, 'Graph_KG.rdf_edges': 2, 'Graph_KG.rdf_labels': 3, 'Graph_KG.rdf_namespaces': 0, 'Graph_KG.rdf_props': 6, 'Graph_KG.rdf_reifications': 0, 'Graph_KG.relationship_mappings': 0, 'Graph_KG.table_mappings': 0} and failed_rows {}. First SELECT * columns {'docs': None, 'nodes': ['node_id', 'graph_id', 'created_at'], 'rdf_edges': ['graph_id', 's', 'p', 'o_id', 'qualifiers', 'ekey'], 'rdf_labels': ['graph_id', 's', 'label'], 'rdf_props': ['graph_id', 's', 'key', 'val']} (P-1801 confirmed live).

findings.title: Edge vectors lose their graph and metadata in a snapshot
findings.intended: SNP-B1.18 (edge vectors keep their graph and notes); Graph_KG.kg_EdgeEmbeddings is UNIQUE (graph_id, s, p, o_id) with metadata (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:455-464).
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-edge-routes, part b): a kg_EdgeEmbeddings row of graph c18L with metadata, planted by SQL (the shape the table's key and metadata column exist for; the pin's own writer sends named-graph edge vectors to routes, part a), [['c18L', 'c18:l1', '{"m": 1}']]; archived as [{'emb': '1,2,3,4', 'o_id': 'c18:l2', 'p': 'R', 's': 'c18:l1'}] (no graph_id, no metadata); after deleting it and a merge restore: [['', 'c18:l1', 'None']].
findings.remedy: Export and restore graph_id and metadata; match on the full key.
findings.notes: At the pin store_edge_embedding(graph=<named>) writes a routed kg_eemb_ table, not kg_EdgeEmbeddings (c18-live-edge-vectors), so the legacy-table path concerns rows written before routing or by SQL; the routed path has its own, larger defect F-C1804.

findings.title: A merge restore overwrites temporal aggregates instead of combining them
findings.intended: SNP-B4.6 (after a merge restore the timed summaries still match the timed events); TemporalIndex.cls:96-125.
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-aggregates): bucket 1700001000 with 2 archived events and a third live one; aggregate count before merge 3 / window 3; after merge restore aggregate 2 / window 3.
findings.remedy: Rebuild touched buckets and tlast after a merge (RebuildBucketAggregate, RebuildLatest) or refuse overlapping merges.

findings.title: Graph.KG.Snapshot.ImportGlobals loads any global file without the allow-list
findings.intended: SNP-X5.1 (every way to load globals keeps to the restore allow-list); snapshot.py:412-422 (an archive is a file anyone can write).

findings.title: The HTTP snapshot endpoint can write two snapshots to one path
findings.intended: Each save produces its own archive (POST /admin/snapshot answers the path it wrote).
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-http-endpoint): two POSTs in one second answered [200, 200] with paths ['/home/ziniu_wu_g5labs_ai/runs/iris-vector-graph-playbook-uplift-20261113/completion-audit/breadth-c/18/archives/ivg_snapshot_1794611107.snapshot', '/home/ziniu_wu_g5labs_ai/runs/iris-vector-graph-playbook-uplift-20261113/completion-audit/breadth-c/18/archives/ivg_snapshot_1794611107.snapshot']; the file holds created_ts 1794611107088 of the second (save timestamps [1794611107076, 1794611107088]).
findings.remedy: Use a unique name (uuid or ms + counter) and refuse to overwrite.

findings.title: save_snapshot archives writes that never commit
findings.intended: decisions.md HD-1802 (working): claim a consistent snapshot only with quiescent writers or a verified snapshot/epoch protocol, and declare the quiet-writer premise for the current exporter; SNP-Q1.17.
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-dirty-export): another connection opened a transaction (TLEVEL 1) and created c18:ghost; save_snapshot ran; the writer rolled back; the DB holds 0 ghost rows, the archive holds {'kg_lines': [{'k': ['label', '0', 'C18Ghost', 'c18:ghost'], 'v': ''}], 'nodes': [{'created_at': '2026-11-13T23:05:06', 'graph_id': '', 'node_id': 'c18:ghost'}], 'rdf_props': [{'graph_id': '', 'key': 'p', 's': 'c18:ghost', 'val': 'uncommitted'}, {'graph_id': '', 'key': 'id', 's': 'c18:ghost', 'val': 'c18:ghost'}]}. Model: cmc-snap-as-built-committed (expected-violation, 36 states, exhaustive within bounds), cmc-snap-as-built-dangling (expected-violation, 63 states, exhaustive within bounds) (an edge archived without its endpoint), reviewed export gate cmc-snap-reviewed (pass, 65 states, exhaustive within bounds), control cmc-snap-ctl-gate (expected-violation, 36 states, exhaustive within bounds), witness cmc-snap-wit (expected-violation, 41 states, exhaustive within bounds). Neither USER_GUIDE.md:1151-1168 nor ADMIN_GUIDE.md:975-1010 declares a quiet-writer premise; the docstring says only 'reads only' (snapshot.py:803).
findings.remedy: Document the quiet-writer premise (HD-1802) and refuse or warn when transactions are open; or export under a namespace-wide export gate that writers respect.
findings.notes: Intent: HD-1802 is a working assumption; the observation (an archive can hold content that never existed, which a restore then makes real) is beyond 'not point in time' and holds under any reading.

findings.title: restore_snapshot drops a global line it cannot write without raising or counting it
findings.intended: SNP-X2.14 (a native index that cannot be written stops the restore; the error says what is done); restore docstring snapshot.py:1088-1094 ('A global it cannot write ... raises RuntimeError').
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-swallowed-lines): an archive with ^IVG.GraphMode lines ['{"k": ["c18x"], "v": "1"}', '{"k": [""], "v": "1"}', '{"k": ["c18y", ""], "v": "1"}']; the bad subscripts set directly over the Native API -> {'[""]': 'RuntimeError: <SUBSCRIPT>', '["c18y", ""]': 'RuntimeError: <SUBSCRIPT>'}; merge restore answered {'failed_rows': {}, 'restored_globals': ['IVG.GraphMode'], 'restored_layers': ['globals'], 'restored_tables': {}, 'snapshot_ts': 1794612073559} (error None); the good line was written: {'c18x': 1}. Source: _import_global_from_ndjson catches every per-line exception with logger.debug (snapshot.py:1665-1683); the unit test test_restore_raises_on_a_global_it_cannot_write patches the whole method to raise (tests/unit/test_460_r271_snapshot_raises.py:156-163), so the per-line path is untested.
findings.remedy: Count failed lines in failed_rows (per global) or raise as documented; a test with a line IRIS refuses.

findings.title: Graph.KG.Snapshot's unused file helpers read, write and delete server files for any Native API caller
findings.intended: ADMIN_GUIDE.md:450-473 grants the least-privilege reading role %Native_ClassExecution:U; nothing in the product needs server file access through IVG classes (no caller of ReadFileChunk/WriteFileChunk/DeleteDir/ExportGlobals).
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-file-helpers, as _SYSTEM): FileExists('/etc/hostname') = 1, GetFileSize = 33, ReadFileChunk returned 'ivg-playbook-20261113-audit-iris\n'. Source: WriteFileChunk (Snapshot.cls:49-57) writes any path, DeleteDir (:64-68) runs RemoveDirectoryTree on any path, ExportGlobals (:4-22) writes any global to any directory, all as the IRIS server's OS user, with no IVG check. Whether a user holding only the documented reading role can call them was not run: it needs a new IRIS user and role on the audit container (blocked-access: Security.Users/Roles changes are container configuration).
findings.remedy: Delete the file and global helpers (no product caller), or restrict them to an admin role and an allow-listed folder.
findings.notes: Extends F-1806 from loading globals to arbitrary server file read/write/delete. Confidence medium: the reading-role reachability rests on ADMIN_GUIDE's grants and IRIS's resource model (file I/O is not resource-protected), not on a live call as that role.

findings.title: A snapshot carries no routed edge vectors (kg_eemb_ tables): a restore loses them silently
findings.intended: ADMIN_GUIDE.md:984-986 (a snapshot holds kg_EdgeEmbeddings and each routed embedding table the registry names); SNP-I1 (each store is copied or its omission explained); SNP-B1.18.
findings.observed: Live (c18-live-edge-vectors, c18-live-edge-routes part a): store_edge_embedding(graph='c18w') wrote route [['kg_eemb_cb5b098c95e72cdb', 'c18w', 'edge', '4']] with 1 row(s); the archive's members are ['metadata.json', 'sql/Graph_KG_nodes.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_rdf_edges.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_rdf_labels.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_rdf_props.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_rdf_reifications.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_docs.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_embedding_registry.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_code_crosswalk.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_rdf_namespaces.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_table_mappings.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_relationship_mappings.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_fhir_bridges.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_kg_NodeEmbeddings.ndjson', 'sql/Graph_KG_kg_EdgeEmbeddings.ndjson', 'globals/KG.ndjson', 'globals/NKG.ndjson'] (no kg_eemb_ file, no routed-table entry; the registry row is archived); after a replacing restore (failed_rows {}) the registry holds [['kg_eemb_cb5b098c95e72cdb', 'c18w', 'edge', 'present']], the route table exists: 0, rows: None; edge_vector_search on the graph: []. Source: routed_export_plan keeps only names is_routed_embedding_table accepts, node routes kg_emb_<16 hex> (snapshot.py:299-344; security.py:58-68 'False for an edge route'), and no other code exports or recreates kg_eemb_ tables.
findings.remedy: Plan and export edge routes (is_routed_edge_embedding_table) with their width and kind, recreate them on restore, and count a registry row whose table could not be restored as failed.
findings.notes: Data loss: after a replacing restore the graph's edge vectors are gone and the report is complete-looking.
